title: Heat Capacities of Gases and Solids
topicTitle: Heat capacities of gases and solids
notes: **Molar heat capacity at constant volume $C_V$:** heat required to raise 1 mole of gas by 1 K at fixed volume. For monatomic gases: $C_V = \frac{3}{2}R$.
**Molar heat capacity at constant pressure $C_P$:** heat required at fixed pressure. $C_P = C_V + R$ because the gas must do expansion work against the external pressure.
**Diatomic gases:** at ordinary temperatures, $C_V = \frac{5}{2}R$ and $C_P = \frac{7}{2}R$ because rotational modes are also active. At high temperatures, vibrational modes contribute further.

**Dulong-Petit law:** the molar heat capacity of most solid elements at room temperature is about $3R \approx 25\,\text{J/mol}\cdot\text{K}$. This comes from 3 quadratic degrees of freedom per atom (one for each axis), each contributing $k_B$ per atom or $R$ per mole.

**Why solids have similar $C$:** despite different atomic masses and stiffness, all solids have the same number of atoms per mole, and each atom contributes equally to heat capacity at high temperature.
